slide_name: Landslide at Vaivakawn, Aizwal District, Mizoram on 09th June 2023
raw_description: A landslide occurred on 09.06.2023 at Vaivakawn Veng, Aizawl, Aizawl District (23° 44' 29.43"N; 92° 42' 28.29"E) caused i) road blockage on NH 54 for three days, ii) complete burial of one pucca house under construction, iii) dismantling of one pucca house, iv) evacuation of one house and v) displaced six families. Heavy and continuous rainfall on the night of 08.06.2023 and early morning of 09.06.2023 triggered this failure. The main causal factors for this event is the seepage of water from the nala along the openings in joint planes, cut slope and excavation on both toe and crown leading to widening of joints aiding in destabilization of the slope.

slide_name: Landslide at Pyndengrei Village, West Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya on 17th June 2023
raw_description: A landslide occurred at Pyndengrei locality (25°31’44.45” N; 91°15’42.79” E) within Nongstoin town, West Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya in the wee hours of 17th June 2023. The debris slide claimed lives of two minor siblings, injured 3 persons and partially destroyed one wooden house. Excavation of natural slope at about 82 ° in highly weathered Granite and untreated slope cut are the causative factors for the landslide which was triggered due to heavy rainfall (223 mm.).

slide_name: Landslide at Dhirenpara, Fatasil hill, Kamrup Metro District, Assam on 17th June 2023
raw_description: A landslide occurred on 17th June 2023 in Dhirenpara area which lies in the eastern part of Fatasil Hill, Kamrup (Metro) district, Assam (26º09'01.935" N, 91º43'40.733" E). Thick section of weak overburden material, multi-tier slope cutting, haphazard flow of surface water flow during incessant rainfall, inadequate retaining wall and surcharge load from civil structures are the main causal factors that led to earth slide killing one person. The triggering factor is attributed to incessant rainfall preceding the incidence.

slide_name: Landslide in Lumjingsuk Block, Madanryting, East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya in July 2023
raw_description: A minor landslide occurred in Lumjinsuk locality (Block–A) of Madanryting, Shillong, East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya (18° 55’ 58.9’’ N, 73° 14’ 4.1’’ E) in July 2023. Houses have been constructed on modified slope where domestic drainage seeping into backslope led to oversaturation of overburden material. The incessant rainfall also added in the development of pore water pressure resulting in a minor slope failure. Cracks are observed in the house located beside an old slide scar making it vulnerable to slope failure. The discharge of domestic waste water should be channelised. The natural drainage course should be maintained and kept hindrance free. Construction of toe support and breast wall are advised to stabilise the houses.

slide_name: Landslide between Chumukedima-Ghaspani along NH 29, Dimapur, Nagaland (8th Sept 2021)
raw_description: A rock fall occurred near Patkai bridge between Chumukedima- Ghaspani along NH-29, (25.782° N, 93.802° E), on 08.09.2021 and blocked NH – 29 due to high rainfall.

slide_name: Landslide at Jibalgre, West Garo Hills District, Meghalaya on 9th June 2022
raw_description: A debris slide occurred at Jibalgre village (25°22’53.88” N, 90°03’37.22” E), West Garo Hills District, Meghalaya on 9th June 2022. The slide destroyed one house and killed three persons while injuring two people. Incessant rainfall from 5th to 10th June 2022 triggered the slide. Unplanned hill slope cutting coupled with oversaturation of the highly weathered slope forming materials is the major causative factor for this slide.

slide_name: Landslide at Laitlarem, East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya on 15th June 2022
raw_description: Three landslides (Debris slides) occurred at Laitlarem village under Mawphlang Community and Rural Development Block, East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya on 15th June, 2022. The area experienced heavy and incessant rainfall in the preceding days which is attributed as the triggering factor for these debris slides. Four lives were lost and five persons injured during this event. Total destruction of the house was also noticed. Unplanned hill slope cutting for road construction coupled with oversaturation of highly weathered slope forming materials are the major causative factors.

slide_name: Landslide at Lumshnong, East Jaintia Hills District, Meghalaya on 15th June 2022
raw_description: A debris slide occurred at Lumshnong area (25°09’50.42” N, 92°23’13.3” E) located on the NH-6 road, East Jaintia Hills district of Meghalaya on 15th June 2022. A part of road has slid down which has resulted into blockage of communication along National Highway-6, triggered by heavy rainfall in the preceding days. An artificial depression had formed due to the unsystematic dumping of quarry material in the upslope portion where rain water accumulated. The sudden release of this water led to the oversaturation of the filled material and caused a portion of the road below to wash away.

slide_name: Landslide at Siju, South Garo Hills District, Meghalaya on 17th June 2022
raw_description: A Debris Slide triggered by incessant rainfall has occurred at Siju (25°21’39.72” N, 90°38’49.23” E), South Garo Hills, Meghalaya on 17th June 2022. The occurrence of this landslide was attributed to the factors viz. i) Unscientific slope cutting without adequate toe support and ii) Oversaturation of highly weathered slope forming material during the heavy downpour. It was reported that one person was killed and two kids were injured in this landslide event.

slide_name: Landslide at Baghmara, South Garo Hills District, Meghalaya on 17th June 2022
raw_description: Two debris slides occurred at Baghmara (25°12’45.86” N, 90°37’55.78” E and 25°12’36.80” N, 90°37’55.93” E), South Garo Hills, Meghalaya on 17th June 2022 triggered by incessant rainfall from 13th to 17th June 2022. The casual factors includes slope cutting without providing adequate toe support and oversaturation of slope forming material during rainfall. Three casualties along with complete destruction of a house was reported due to this landslide.

slide_name: Landslide at Nongal Bibra, South Garo Hills District, Meghalaya on 17th June 2022
raw_description: Two landslide events occurred at Nongal Bibra, South Garo Hills, Meghalaya on 17th June 2022. Heavy and incessant rainfall during the period from 4th to 17th June was the triggering factor. Steeply sloping topography, toe cutting coupled with weak slope forming materials and the oversaturation of slope forming material during the heavy rainfall leads to this slope stability issue at Nongal Bibra. Four houses were reported damaged during this event.

slide_name: Assessment of Landslide Prone Areas under Sohbar Sirdarship, East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya August 2022
raw_description: A preliminary assessment of landslide prone areas (25°12’47.6” N, 91°45’2.4” E) under Sohbar Sirdarship, East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya was carried out on 30th August 2022. During this study, the vulnerability of the slope areas and the risk associated with it has been evaluated and suitable stability measures as per the site conditions were suggested.

slide_name: Landslide at Saitbakon, Pynursia Area Along Shillong- Dawki Road, East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya (4th April 2022)
locality: Saitbakon, Pynursia Area Along Shillong- Dawki Road
raw_description: Two rockslides occurred on 4th April 2022 in Saitabakon (25.295° N, 91.932° E) and Pynursia (25.345° N, 91.891° E) area of East Khasi hills District, Meghalaya triggered by heavy rainfall. Both the slides occurred due to wedge failure, partially damaging the road.

slide_name: Landslide at Umblai and Lynshing Village, East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya (4th April 2022)
raw_description: Three debris slides occurred in East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya on 4th April 2022. Two debris slides occurred at Umblai (25.358° N, 91.972° E ; 25.359° N, 91.974° E) while one debris slide occurred at Lynshing village (25.396° N, 91.992° E) and blocked the road at Umblai and Lynshing village. Two people lost their lives due to debris slide at Umblai village.

slide_name: Landslide in Hospital area, Thingsulthliah, Aizwal district, Mizoram (9th Oct 2021)
raw_description: A debris slide (Lat: 23.684° N, Lon: 92.857° E) at Hospital Area, Vengsang locality, Thingsulthliah village, Aizawl district occurred on 09.10.2021 due to high continuous rainfall from 08.10.2021 since 23:00 hrs until 02:00 hrs of 09.10. 2021 and caused death of two persons and damaged a two-storey house.

slide_name: Landslide, near Tourist Lodge colony under Wokha town, Wokha District, Nagaland (18th Sept 2021)
raw_description: A landslide occurred on 18.09.21 at E-khel, Wokha village (26.107° N, 94.253° E) triggered by incessant rainfall resulted in the slope failure of a fishery pond located on the upslope thereby damaging a building in the downslope.

slide_name: Landslides near Umiam view point along NH-40, East Khasi hills district, Meghalaya (Sept 2021)
raw_description: Three landslides (one rock slide (25.650° N, 91.899° E), two Debris slides (25.649° N, 91.899° E)) occurred in a stretch of approximately 600m along NH-40 between Umiam viewpoint to Guwahati triggered by heavy rainfall.

slide_name: Landslide at North-West of Sohiong village along NH-44E (by pass road), East Khasi hills district, Meghalaya (Sept 2021)
raw_description: A landslide occurred at 1.2 Km north-west of Sohiong Village (25.510° N, 91.704° E) during September 2021 and blocked the drainage along the road.

slide_name: Landslide at Upper Burtuk, Gangtok, East District, Sikkim (6th June 2021)
raw_description: A debris slide incidence has happened on the morning of 06th June 2021 at Upper Burtuk (27.358° N, 88.621° E), Gangtok, East District, Sikkim partially blocking the road. It is inferred that the slide may have taken place due to the saturation of overburden material leading to reduction in shear strength of the soil.

slide_name: Landslides at Tibetan Jhora, Gangtok, East District, Sikkim (8th June 2021)
raw_description: A debris slide occurred on 8th June 2021 at Tibetan Jhora, Siche (27.342° N, 88.607° E), Gangtok, East District, Sikkim causing the death of one person and damaging a house. It is inferred that the slide may have taken place due to the super saturation of overburden material, which mainly consisted of debris mass.

slide_name: Landslide at Tashi View Point-I, Gangtok, East District, Sikkim (6th June 2021)
raw_description: A debris slide occurred in the early morning of 06th June 2021 near Tashi View Point (27.370° N, 88.616° E), Gangtok, East District, Sikkim on Gangtok-Kabi Road partially blocked the road communication. The slide may have taken place due to reduction in the shear strength of the soil caused by super saturation of overburden material due to heavy rainfall.

slide_name: Landslide at Tamang Gompa , Gangtok, East District, Sikkim (8th June 2021)
raw_description: A debris slide occurred in the night of 8th June 2021 near Tamang Gompa (27.339° N, 88.620° E), Gangtok, East District, Sikkim damaging and blocking the road affecting communication. Heavy rainfall along with anthropogenic activities due to construction on the crown portion of the slide may have created suitable condition for slide to occur by reduction in shear strength of the rock mass due to oversaturation.

slide_name: Landslide at Swastik-II, Gangtok, East District, Sikkim (6th June 2021)
raw_description: A debris slide occurred on the early morning of 06th June 2021 at Swastik area near to the Black Cat (27.353° N, 88.617° E), Gangtok, East District, Sikkim partially blocking the road and affecting communication. The debris slide is triggered by heavy rainfall, it looks meagre in extent but the presence of additional large boulders resting along the slope, makes it susceptible to further landslides in future.

slide_name: Landslide at Swastik Market, Gangtok, East District, Sikkim (7th June 2021)
raw_description: A debris slide occurred on 7th June 2021 at Swastik Market (27.357° N, 88.618° E), Gangtok, East District, Sikkim blocking NH-10 for several hours and partially damaging a house. The debris slide is triggered by heavy rainfall causing super saturation of thick overburden (Soil) cover.

slide_name: Landslide at Lower Burtuk, Gangtok, East District, Sikkim (6th June 2021)
raw_description: A debris slide occurred on early morning of 6th June 2021 at Lower Burtuk (27.358° N, 88.620° E) , Indra by-pass, Gangtok, East District, Sikkim partially blocking the road and affecting communication. The slide was triggered by reduction in strength of slope material due to super saturation of overburden material caused by heavy rainfall.

slide_name: Landslide at Development area-I Gangtok, East District, Sikkim (6th June 2021)
raw_description: A debris slide occurred at Development Area- I (27.339° N, 88.609° E, Near Little Pixes School), Gangtok, East District, Sikkim on 06.06.2021 partially blocking the road and affecting communication. Heavy rainfall and flowing condition on the slope provided suitable condition for the slide to occur due to reduction in shear strength of the soil along with anthropogenic activities.

slide_name: Landslide at Bhojogari- I, Gangtok, East District, Sikkim (6th June 2021)
raw_description: A debris slide occurred in the early morning of 06th June 2021 at Bhojogari (27.364° N, 88.621° E) on Indira Bye Pass Road, Gangtok, East District, Sikkim partially blocking the road. The steep slope around the landslide affected area with loose debris and soil aided by heavy rainfall may have led to slope failure.

slide_name: Landslides at Bhairabkunda, Udalguri District, Arunachal Pradesh (28th April 21)
raw_description: Two landslides occurred near embankment of river in Bhairabkunda, Udalguri District, Arunachal Pradesh (28th April 21). Both the slides (Lat: 26.89074° N, Lon: 92.12068° E) are debris slides that were reactivated by an earthquake measuring 6.4 on the Richter scale that occurred on 28/04/21. Transverse cracks with an opening of about 0.5cm are observed at the zone of accumulation of the slide for an about 1 to 2 m in length at one of the landslide. Anthropogenic activities including sand and rock quarrying at the toe of the hill slope might have been one of the possible causative factor for the slope failure.

slide_name: Landslide around Longmai-Khumji Noney Area, Noney District, Manipur (June-July, 2020)
raw_description: The Longmai landslide occurred during the last week of June 2020 along the upslope of NH-37, about 500 meters from Noney Bazar towards Imphal. The Khumji Noney Slide occurred about 100 meters from Noney Bazaar towards Jiribam on the NH-37, Imphal-Jiribam road. Excessive cutting of the slope for construction and water seepage in the upslope portion are the main geo-scientific causes of the landslides.

slide_name: Landslide around Mao Town, Senapati District, Manipur (July, 2020)

district_conflict.title: Landslide around Mao Town, Senapati District, Manipur (July, 2020)

raw_description: The Mao landslide affected an area of about 0.6 sq.km. in Manipur, posing immense risk to critical road infrastructure and affecting residential and commercial buildings along NH-2 due to tensional cracks and subsidence of the road bench. The area is part of an old landslide zone with thick unconsolidated debris above the in-situ bedrock.

slide_name: Landslide at Tigdo Village, Papumpare District, Arunachal Pradesh on 10th July, 2020
raw_description: A landslide occurred at Tigdo Village under Doimukh circle, Papumpare district, Arunachal Pradesh, due to heavy rain. A house was totally damaged, and four persons of a family were buried, causing property loss. Continuous heavy rainfall and anthropogenic activities like deforestation and high-angle slope cutting contributed to the landslide.

slide_name: Landslide at Donyi Colony, Papumpare District, Arunachal Pradesh on 25th June, 2020
raw_description: A landslide occurred at Donyi Colony, Itanagar, Papumpare district, Arunachal Pradesh, due to incessant heavy rainfall. The slope failure was attributed to oversaturation of unconsolidated slope forming material composed mostly of sand, silt, and clay, coupled with anthropogenic activities like deforestation and unplanned construction.

slide_name: Landslides in Cachar, Hailakandi and Karimganj Districts, Assam (June, 2020)
raw_description: In the first week of June 2020, several parts of Barak Valley comprising three districts of Assam, namely Cachar, Hailakandi, and Karimganj, were affected by eight landslides triggered by incessant heavy rainfall. Over-saturation of overburden material due to heavy rainfall caused rapid downslope movement along cut slope faces.

slide_name: Landslide at Jowai, Kabi Village, West Jaintia Hills District, Meghalaya on 26 May, 2020
raw_description: Eight landslides of varying dimensions occurred on 26th May 2020 at different localities within the Jowai Township in Meghalaya, affecting residential areas. Heavy antecedent rainfall increased surface runoff beyond the drainage capacity, leading to soil super-saturation and subsequent failure.

slide_name: Landslide at Mawlai-Umjapung, East Khasi Hills District, Meghalaya on 21 May, 2020
raw_description: A landslide occurred at Mawlai-Umjapung, about 50 m East of NH-40 on 21st May 2020, partially burying a house. Incessant rainfall led to the collapse of a poorly constructed retaining wall onto a house, rendering a family homeless. The slope, modified for settlement, is composed of thick overburden of highly oxidized cohesive clayey soil.

slide_name: Landslide at Kabi Village, North Sikkim District, Sikkim on 24 May, 2020
raw_description: A landslide got reactivated on 24th May 2020, near upper Kabi Village area on the state highway, adjacent to the border between East and North Sikkim Districts of Sikkim, causing disruption of traffic. The landslide is characterized by wedge failure along with falling of bedrock material along a steep slope (>70°), due to the action of gravity and flow of water through weak planes.

slide_name: Landslide at Dhare & Sitala, Kabi Village, North Sikkim District, Sikkim on 24 May, 2020
raw_description: Two landslides occurred on 24th May 2020, about 04 km away from Kabi Village towards Gangtok on North Sikkim Highway (NH 310A). Both landslides are characterized by unconsolidated soil and debris material, located in close proximity to a NE-SW trending Regional Fault. Improper irrigation practices and toe erosion from unplanned road cutting are contributing factors.

slide_name: Landslide at Bhandari Town, Wokha District, Nagaland in November 2019
raw_description: A landslide was observed about 2 km southeast of Bhandari Town, Wokha District, Nagaland, during fieldwork in November 2019. The landslide occurred on the western slope of a hill and had been reactivated multiple times since July 2017. The slope angle is moderate (20°-25°), and a poorly constructed retaining wall collapsed onto a house.

slide_name: Landslide at NIT Campus, Dimapur District, Nagaland on 26th October, 2019
raw_description: A landslide occurred on the northwestern flank of NIT campus, Dimapur, Nagaland, on 26th October 2019, due to continuous rainfall. The slide damaged half-constructed RCC buildings and affected other RCC buildings/quarters belonging to NIT. The area is characterized by super-saturated soil/debris slopes.
